faqs.a: A commission is a percentage of the sales you generate. This calculator multiplies your total sales by your rate and adds any base salary. It assumes one flat rate — if your plan has tiered slabs (for example 5% up to a target, 8% above it), calculate each slab separately.

Base plus commission gives you income stability with upside; commission-only gives unlimited upside with zero safety net. Most people earn more total under base-plus-commission in their first year, then outgrow it as their sales pipeline matures.
faqs.q: Base salary plus commission, or commission only?

faqs.a: Ask for it in writing before you start, including the rate, what counts as a sale (booked vs paid), when it is paid, and what happens to pending deals if you leave. Verbal promises in sales jobs are worth exactly nothing.
faqs.q: How do I negotiate a better commission rate?

faqs.a: Usually not, until the customer pays. Most plans pay commission on collected revenue, not booked orders, and some include a clawback if the customer cancels within a window. Check whether your plan says booked, billed, or collected.
faqs.q: Do I earn commission on a sale before the customer pays?

faqs.a: Common sales roles pay 5–15% in retail and real estate services, 10–30% in insurance and financial products, and 20–50% in high-margin agency or freelance work. Anything far outside these bands deserves a careful look at the fine print.
faqs.q: What is a typical commission rate?

faqs.a: In most countries, including India, commission is treated as salary or professional income and taxed at your slab rate, with TDS often deducted. The calculator shows pre-tax earnings — your take-home will be lower.

commission-calculator.formula:
Commission = total sales x (rate / 100).
Total earnings = base salary + commission.
Example: 500,000 x 7% = 35,000; plus 20,000 base = 55,000.
howTo: Enter your total sales for the period.
Enter your commission rate as a percentage.
Add your base salary, if you have one (leave 0 for commission-only).
Read your commission and total earnings instantly.
keyFacts: Commission is pay linked to results: a fixed percentage of the sales you close.

commission-calculator.quickAnswer: On ₹500,000 of sales at a 7% commission rate with a ₹20,000 base salary, you earn ₹35,000 in commission and ₹55,000 in total. Commission is simply sales times your rate — the calculator adds your base on top so you see the full picture in one number.
commission-calculator.tagline: Work out exactly what your sales earn you — commission, base salary, and total pay.
commission-calculator.workedExample:
Sales ₹500,000, rate 7%, base salary ₹20,000:
1. Commission = 500,000 x 7 / 100 = ₹35,000.
2. Total earnings = 35,000 + 20,000 = ₹55,000.
3. Effective rate on sales = 35,000 / 500,000 x 100 = 7%.
